solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dogs responsible for mother's quarrels

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother, with the possessive S
tiffs are petty quarrels

explanation.surface: Someone blames a set of dogs for a mother's rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a breed of large, powerful guard dog.

clue.text: A venue for a match away from home

parts.note: a sports match is played on a field

explanation.surface: Describing where an away fixture is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means at a distance, away from one's home ground, as in 'far afield'.

clue.text: Giant bird on a pole

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
N stands for the North Pole

explanation.surface: An enormous bird perched on top of a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth, so a titan is any giant.

clue.text: Out of one's mind

parts.note: read not as 'mad' but literally: something no longer held in one's memory

explanation.surface: A description of someone who has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has slipped out of memory, literally out of the mind.

clue.text: Company in rush to get cat

indicators.note: the company abbreviation sits inside the word for a rush

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush forward

explanation.surface: A firm hurries to acquire a pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat here is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip, and the cat-o'-nine-tails is a many-thonged whip.

clue.text: Follow Rex inside to make certain

indicators.note: the king's letter is placed within the word for follow

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on as a result
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Bringing the king in to guarantee something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to guarantee or make sure that something happens.

clue.text: Concluded many may be in dire need

indicators.note: dire as in dreadful, so these letters are in a dreadful mess and get rearranged

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number

explanation.surface: Many people may be desperately in need, it was decided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' looks like a description of the need but is the anagram signal working on D and NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ended is a past form meaning finished or brought to a close.

clue.text: Upset friends, content to be casual

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pals are friends
content means satisfied, happy

explanation.surface: Unsettled friends who are still content to take things easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy means carefree to the point of being careless, a casual attitude.

clue.text: Set price being fixed, proceeds

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A price being set and agreed before the sale goes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are the money taken in, the takings or proceeds of a sale.

clue.text: It may be carried on, though by-laws forbid it

definitions.meaning: a covered couch or stretcher borne on people's shoulders
rubbish dropped in public places, banned by local rules

explanation.surface: Something carried along that local laws nonetheless prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is both a portable couch or stretcher and discarded rubbish in public places.

clue.text: Regulation I ignored in making guns

indicators.note: the letter I is ignored, so it is dropped from the word

parts.note: an ordinance is an official regulation or decree

explanation.surface: A rule being disregarded when making weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military artillery and weaponry, especially big guns.

clue.text: Result of strikes in the metal industry

definitions.text: Result of strikes in the metal industry

parts.words: Result of strikes in the metal industry
parts.note: not industrial action but hammer blows on metal, which produce a loud ringing din

explanation.surface: The aftermath of industrial walkouts among metalworkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is the loud ringing noise of metal being struck.

clue.text: Hilda is upset about a bloomer

indicators.note: Hilda is thrown into disorder along with the letter beside her, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Hilda is distressed about some blunder she made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant grown for its flowers, so a bloomer.

clue.text: Bound to fight bravely?

parts.note: braves are Native American warriors, so fighting 'bravely' means as a brave would, heading into battle

explanation.surface: Someone certain to put up a courageous fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hostile and ready for a fight, from Native American warriors' routes to battle.

clue.text: Bound to be glad I came round

indicators.note: the letters are brought round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to say they were pleased to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' is the definition, and 'to be glad I' is all fodder despite reading like a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligated means bound by duty or obliged to do something.

clue.text: Atrophied form of the goddess of love

indicators.note: another form of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wasted, shrunken version of the love goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: 100's too old for insurance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
overage means beyond the permitted age

explanation.surface: A centenarian is considered too old to get insured.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the protection an insurance policy gives.

clue.text: Healthily, Ron gets involved in congress

indicators.note: involved as in tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Ron, in good health, takes part in a political assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congress' looks political but means sexual intercourse; the answer is the idiom for a romp, often outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress can mean sexual union, and the idiom is slang for having sex.

clue.text: Lock-keeper comes out of the rain

indicators.note: the letters emerge in a different arrangement from what they were in

explanation.surface: A canal lock-keeper stepping in from the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-keeper' suggests a canal worker; the lock is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine net that holds locks of hair in place.

clue.text: Respect maiden in a grave environment

indicators.note: the maiden is placed within the surrounding letters
the other letters form the setting around the maiden

parts.note: grave means serious, dire
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Paying tribute to a young woman in solemn surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard, to respect them.

clue.text: Union measure

definitions.meaning: an alliance or association of groups
an old unit of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A trade union taking some action.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is both an alliance of members and an old measure of distance.

clue.text: Eastern lake found in the Midwest? Strange

parts.note: Lake Erie borders Ohio and other Midwestern states

explanation.surface: An odd discovery of an eastern lake in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Puritan club team

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A strait-laced religious sports club's team.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironsides were Cromwell's Puritan cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironside was one of Cromwell's Puritan troopers, hence a Puritan.

clue.text: Cuttlefish very good in sea setting

indicators.note: the pious letters go within the sea
the sea forms the setting round the other letters

parts.note: PI is short for pious, very good

explanation.surface: A fine cuttlefish displayed in its natural sea habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the cuttlefish, and the genus name for it, source of the brown ink.

clue.text: Sort of alibi that cannot be forged

definitions.meaning: an alibi that is unshakeable and cannot be disproved
a metal too brittle to be hammered into shape

explanation.surface: An alibi that is impossible to fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' hints at fake documents but means shaped by hammering; this metal cracks rather than bends.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron describes an unbreakable alibi and also brittle iron that is cast, not forged.

clue.text: Look after little devil causing harm

indicators.note: the word for look follows the little devil

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone minding a mischievous child who causes damage.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it.

clue.text: Point that was put on record

definitions.meaning: a sharp point, as of a pin
the stylus of an old record player rested on the disc

explanation.surface: A remark that was formally put on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle has a sharp point and is also the stylus that played gramophone records.

clue.text: One who hasn't made a score in years

definitions.text: One who hasn't made a score in years

parts.words: One who hasn't made a score in years
parts.note: not a lapsed sportsman, but someone whose age has not yet reached twenty, a score

explanation.surface: A player who hasn't scored for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is aged thirteen to nineteen, short of a score of years.
